== Overview ==
It is enshrined at the south end of the Miyako settlement, west of Miyako Pond. Miyako belonged to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiroshita District}} since ancient times; while early history is unknown, it is thought that the Miyake no Muraji clan of this area enshrined their ancestral deity. It was formerly called Hoya Myōjin.

== Precinct ==
The current shrine buildings were rebuilt after typhoon damage in {{ill|Heisei era|ar|فترة هيسي|br|Oadvezh Heisei|ca|Període Heisei|cdo|Bìng-sìng|ckb|سەردەمی ھێیسێی|cs|Období Heisei|de|Heisei-Zeit|eo|Hejsej-epoko|es|Era Heisei|fa|دوره هیسه‌ای|fi|Heisei-kausi|fr|Ère Heisei|he|תקופת הייסי|hi|हेइसेई युग|hr|Heisei|hu|Heiszei-kor|id|Zaman Heisei|it|Periodo Heisei|ja|平成|ka|ჰეისეის პერიოდი|ko|헤이세이 시대|lt|Heisei laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Heisei|nl|Heiseiperiode|no|Heisei|oc|Heisei|pl|Heisei|pt|Período Heisei|ru|Хэйсэй|sco|Heisei period|simple|Heisei era|sk|Obdobie Heisei|sl|Heisei (obdobje)|su|Heisei|sv|Heisei|th|ยุคเฮเซ|tl|Panahong Heisei|tr|Heisei Dönemi|uk|Хейсей|uz|Heisei|vi|Thời kỳ Bình Thành|zh|平成|zh_classical|平成|zh_min_nan|Pêng-sêng|zh_yue|平成|qid=Q234510}} 9 ({{ill|1997|Q2088|qid=Q2088}}). The honden is an ikken-sha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} with chigi and katsuogi.

== Overview ==
It is located at the southwest edge of the Hozu ring-moat settlement. Although the current site belongs to former {{ill|Toichi district|Q11405036|qid=Q11405036}}, before the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}} it is said to have been in Ita-shiki, about 300 m east of the present location, and moved here along with relocation of the Hozu settlement. In ancient times, the Hozu clan of Mononobe surname is said to have lived in the ring-moat settlement, and this shrine is inferred to have worshiped their ancestral deity.

== Precinct ==
The honden consists of two buildings, north and south honden. The south honden was built in the rare "sumiki-iri {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|es|Kasuga-zukuri|fr|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造|ru|Касуга-дзукури|qid=Q3193781}}" method during the {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}} years (1804-1818).
